Looking for Property in Arlington VA? Here’s How to Win at a Tax Auction

Introduction

Looking to buy property at a lower price in Arlington County, Virginia? Tax deed sales may be your way in. These public auctions happen when property owners haven’t paid their taxes in years. The county then sells these properties to recover the taxes—and you could become the new owner by placing the highest bid.

This guide explains everything you need to know about Arlington County’s tax deed sales, including how to register, how much deposit is needed, and why this could be a great chance for real estate investors.

Brief Overview of Virginia’s Tax Sale Process

In Virginia, most counties—including Arlington—sell tax deeds, not tax liens. This means you are bidding to take full ownership of the property. The sales are court-ordered and happen at random times, not on a regular schedule. Every county has its own rules, so it’s important to stay up-to-date.

Important Details: Arlington County, Virginia Tax Deed Sales

What Makes Virginia Ideal for Tax Deed Investors

Virginia offers several perks for investors:

  • The sale process is run through the courts, making it clear and reliable
  • Once the court approves the sale, you become the owner—no wait time
  • A strong mix of residential and commercial properties available
  • Stable real estate laws make investing safer

Why Arlington County?

Arlington is one of the most popular locations in Northern Virginia. It’s just across the river from Washington, D.C., and has a mix of city living, job opportunities, and historic charm. Homes in the area are in demand, which means buying at auction could lead to solid returns.

Fun Facts About Arlington County

  • Estimated population (2024): 240,900
  • Land area: 25.8 square miles, making it the smallest self-governing county in the U.S.
  • Home to the Pentagon and Arlington National Cemetery
  • Over 600 restaurants, 148 parks, and many outdoor trails
  • 77.7% of residents have a bachelor’s degree or higher
  • Population forecast for 2050: 311,200
  • One of the longest escalators in the world is at Rosslyn Metro Station
  • For more facts, visit the Arlington County Profile

Attractions and Economic Highlights

Popular Attractions
Arlington is filled with museums, public parks, theaters, historic sites, and event spaces. You’re also just minutes from all that Washington, D.C. offers.

Transportation
Arlington is well connected with Metro stations, major highways, bus lines, and bike trails.

Economy
Major industries include government, defense, tech, consulting, and education.

Community Appeal
The county is known for its clean streets, civic involvement, walking trails, family-friendly parks, and eco-friendly growth plans.

Auction Process: How It Works

  1. Register either online or in person.
  2. Bidding happens in person or at ForSaleAtAuction.biz.
  3. If you win, you must pay a 25% deposit or at least $1,000, whichever is more.
  4. A 5% buyer’s premium is added to your final bid.
  5. Once the court confirms the sale, you have 15 days to pay the rest.
  6. Properties are sold as-is, with no refunds or guarantees.

You can read the full details on the Arlington Tax Sale Page.

Maximum Potential Returns

Because you’re buying the deed to the property (not just a lien), there’s a chance to earn strong returns. If the property is in a great location like Arlington, you could resell it or rent it out for profit.

Open to All Investors

Both local and international investors are welcome to participate in Arlington’s tax deed sales. Just make sure you’re not behind on your own property taxes and you aren’t listed in any local tax lawsuits.

Understanding the Process in Arlington County

These auctions are legal court proceedings. Once you bid and win, you’re agreeing to buy the property—no turning back. That’s why it’s so important to:

  • Visit the property (from the street only)
  • Order a title search
  • Review zoning information
  • Make sure you’re comfortable with the risks

Properties may have issues like no access roads or outstanding liens.

The Importance of Due Diligence

Before you bid, take these steps:

  • Visit the neighborhood
  • Hire someone to check the title history
  • Make sure the land use fits your plans

Skipping these steps can lead to big problems, like legal issues or unusable land.

Buying Over-the-Counter (OTC)

Arlington County does not currently offer OTC sales. All tax deed properties go through auction.

Why Virginia Is a Good Choice for Tax Deed Investors

Economic and Tax Advantages
Virginia has a steady economy and balanced tax system. It’s seen as a low-risk area to invest, especially around the D.C. metro area.

Real Estate Market
Demand in Arlington is high, especially for homes near transit, schools, and job centers.

Pro Tips

  • Sign up for email updates from Taxing Authority Consulting Services
  • Bring cash, cashier’s checks, or money orders—no personal checks
  • Bidders must be in good standing (no unpaid local taxes)
  • For help, call Cathryn Bertram at (804) 545-2377

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I get the property right after the auction?
No. You must wait for the court to confirm the sale before completing your payment.

Can I go inside the property before bidding?
No. You can only view it from the street.

Are these auctions online or in person?
Both. You can bid at forsaleatauction.biz or in person.

Can I get a loan to pay for the property?
No. You must pay the balance yourself within 15 days of court approval.

Can international investors join?
Yes. Anyone can bid if they meet the local requirements.
